To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Java meta-lock algorithm is correct for all values of N and M up to 10,000 and that the XMC model checking approach is a viable alternative to formal verification.
XMC can be successfully used to prove properties of parameterized systems and that the meta-locking technique indeed provides mutual exclusion.
XMC can be used to prove that the meta-locking algorithms provides mutual exclusion and lockout freedom for all values of M and for all values of N up to 1000.
In summary, our research is concerned with
model checking algorithms for concurrent programs.
the following question: how can we verify that a given algorithm is correct, in a way that is independent of the number of threads or the number of objects?
the application of model checking techniques to the verification of highly optimized algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for any values of M, N > 0, the Java meta-lock algorithm is correct.
for M=10 and N<=1000, the algorithm is correct, for all possible interleavings of the threads.
, for the parameter values M=10 and N=10000, the Java meta-lock algorithm ensures that no thread can be starved and that no thread is able to enter a monitor queue more than once.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how to use the XMC model-checker to prove the correctness of the meta-lock algorithm, and how the use of the XMC modelchecker can be integrated with the Java compiler.
XMC is a powerful tool for model checking parameterized systems.
XMC is a very promising model checker for the analysis of concurrent programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the XMC model checking tool can be successfully applied to large, complex Java programs.
model checking can provide a high degree of confidence that a complex algorithm is correct, even in cases where the algorithm is highly parameterized.
the XMC model-checking technology is sufficiently mature to be applied in the context of real-world software.
